summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update36.json → valid=true). Found and recorded material contrary evidence while checking the shutdown-completion finding against the retained tests: the after-shutdown test carries a TODO stating that Barrier, VerifyLeader and GetConfiguration can get stuck when a buffered channel consumes the future and the instance is then shut down (raft_test.go:40-42) — the same mechanism my earlier records derived from the channel capacities, the loop's shutdown branch and the unarmed escape field. So that gap is acknowledged in the repository, not unnoticed. Corrected the existing knowledge id (changed_premise explains the reframing; affected_uses empty since that revision records no uses) and added a successor interpretation for the same question, keeping every earlier opinion alongside it. Three consequences recorded: (1) novelty — for the three named entry points this must be presented as an acknowledged known issue, and the audit rule that a TODO does not create a contract cuts the other way here, since the comment is evidence of maintainer awareness rather than a defence of the behaviour; (2) reach — the acknowledgement is narrower than the code, which also buffers applies (with the buffering option) and leadership transfers, exactly what my earlier correction had added, so that part survives; (3) method — the test's own assertions cover only the enqueue-time case, where operations issued after shutdown fail immediately because those channels are unbuffered, and no retained assertion exercises a request enqueued before shutdown, so the suite neither demonstrates nor excludes the stuck case. Counterevidence kept explicit, including that a maintainer could reasonably treat the acknowledged cases as accepted behaviour for a non-graceful shutdown (weakening the finding to a documented limitation for those three) and that the reach beyond the acknowledgement rests on the code paths, not on the TODO. Nothing was executed.
